posts.title: The Question That Changes Everything in a Boardroom
posts.excerpt: What is the single most powerful thing a board facilitator can do in the first five minutes of a board meeting?

blocks.content:
What is the single most powerful thing a board facilitator can do in the first five minutes of a board meeting?

It's not an icebreaker. It's not a recap of the previous meeting. It's not a review of the agenda.

It's a question the organization genuinely doesn't have the answer to yet.

(Full post to come — the principles in The Genuine Board Leader didn't emerge from a research lab or a business school. They emerged from thousands of boardrooms, hundreds of leadership assessments, and nineteen years of paying close attention to what actually works when leaders are under real pressure making real decisions. This blog is where those principles continue to develop.)

blocks.content:
Nineteen years. Thousands of board meetings. Hundreds of leadership assessments. One discovery:

The leaders and boards that create sustainable competitive advantage aren't the ones with the longest résumés. They're the ones who lead with genuine alignment between who they claim to be and how they actually show up.

The Thread That Runs Through Everything

At the heart of The Genuine Board Leader is a framework developed over two decades of working with leaders at every level of organizational life.

T — Tell Your Story

Lead with authenticity. Your actual story, not the polished version, is your most powerful leadership asset.

O — Optimistic

Choose optimism deliberately. Not as naivety, but as a refusal to let pessimism become your default leadership mode.

U — Unconditional

Build relationships that transcend transactional benefit. Care about people for who they are, not what they can do for you.

C — Care

Show it visibly. Transparently. Genuine care changes how people show up around you.

H — Help

Give it without keeping score. And when help is offered to you, receive it with the same grace you give it.
These five principles are explored in depth in The Genuine Board Leader — and they are available to begin practicing today.

About the Book

The Genuine Board Leader synthesizes the proven principles of three remarkable thinkers — Jim Collins, Simon Sinek, and David Novak — filtered through nineteen years of real-world board governance practice.

This isn't another leadership theory. It's a guide to how genuine leadership actually develops when you're willing to do the work.

Across nineteen chapters, The Genuine Board Leader explores:

  • Why your leadership DNA was installed before you ever entered a boardroom
  • How intentional learners practice excellence as a daily discipline
  • Why your best board member is the one who makes you most uncomfortable
  • How failure becomes your organization's most valuable curriculum
  • Why simplicity is a leadership discipline most organizations violate daily
  • How to build boards that are architectures of character, not collections of credentials
  • What it means to lead as a steward rather than an owner
  • And thirteen more principles that transform how boards function and how leaders develop

pages.seo_description: Founder of Board Developer, author of The Power of Touch, host of the A-Ha Moments podcast — and author of the forthcoming book The Genuine Board Leader.

blocks.content:
About Jim Hayden

Jim Hayden didn't arrive at leadership through a traditional path. He was born on an Air Force base and spent his first eight years living in Asia — the Philippines and Korea — navigating two radically different cultures before he understood what culture meant. Growing up as one of ten of twelve children, he slept on a canvas cot that was folded against the wall every morning because the space was that precious.

He delivered pizzas on the west side of Phoenix. He pursued a significant clinical background. He worked for and ultimately ran Southwest Ambulance, a billion-dollar company with thirteen thousand employees. And in 2007, he founded Board Developer, now one of the nation's foremost board governance and leadership development firms.

Over nineteen years, Hayden has facilitated thousands of board meetings, conducted thousands of leadership assessments through the Hayden Leadership Framework, served on dozens of boards, and founded multiple organizations — including Stop Our Stigma, a nonprofit dedicated to mental health awareness, and gilberttalks.org, a civic engagement platform he founded and stepped back from, which continues to thrive without his direct involvement.

He is the author of The Power of Touch, available on Amazon, a book that established the human connection principles that form the foundation of his leadership philosophy.

His forthcoming book, The Genuine Board Leader, synthesizes principles from Jim Collins, Simon Sinek, and David Novak with nineteen years of real-world governance practice into a guide for leaders who are ready to stop performing and start being.

Hayden hosts the A-Ha Moments podcast, where he has interviewed hundreds of accomplished leaders about the single most transformative moment that shaped their leadership journey. The consistent finding: the most profound leadership moments trace back to childhood.

He divides his time between Tempe, Arizona and Denver, Colorado.

blocks.content:
Watch the Preview

Six Principles That Will Change How You Lead

In this ten-minute preview, Jim Hayden shares six of the nineteen principles at the heart of The Genuine Board Leader:

🎬 Ten-Minute Preview — coming soon

Jim's recorded preview will be embedded here once the Zoom recording is delivered.

• Where leadership actually begins — and why it's almost certainly not where you think.
  • The WAIT acronym — a simple four-letter intervention that transforms how you listen in every room you enter.
  • The attorney with the glasses — a true story about the most valuable board member who had no subject matter expertise whatsoever.
  • The sales leader story — how a board unanimously made the call a CEO couldn't make himself, and why he called it the best board meeting he ever had.
  • TOUCH — the five principles that run through every chapter of the book and every genuine leadership relationship.
  • The Styrofoam cup — what happens when the position is gone and only the person remains.

What You'll Discover in the Full Book

The preview covers six principles. The book covers nineteen. Here's a glimpse of what's waiting:

  • How preparation itself changes how you listen, and the twenty-year note-taking system that proves it
  • Why reflection doesn't work in a quiet room for most leaders, and what to do instead
  • How to build boards that are architectures of character, not collections of credentials
  • The mathematical case for advisory boards: one hundred fifty to two hundred ten years of collective experience sitting around one table
  • Why simplicity is a leadership discipline that most organizations violate every time something goes wrong
  • How to manage technology so it doesn't manage you, and what thousands of hours saved in six months actually looks like
  • What genuine legacy means and how to build something that thrives long after you step back
